1. **Effectiveness rating:** 3

2. **Rationale:**
   The government's plan to support up to 90,000 AI-related employment and work-placement opportunities by 2031 is a commendable initiative aimed at enhancing AI literacy and adoption in Canada. By providing these opportunities, the policy seeks to equip young Canadians with the skills and experience necessary to thrive in the evolving AI economy. This approach aligns with the objectives of the "AI for All" strategy, which targets significant economic growth and increased AI adoption by 2034. ([pm.gc.ca](https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/news/news-releases/2026/06/04/prime-minister-carney-launches-ai-all-canadas-new-national-artificial?utm_source=openai))

   However, the effectiveness of this policy may be limited by several challenges:

   - **Barriers to AI Adoption:** Many Canadian businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), face difficulties in integrating AI due to resource constraints, lack of expertise, and concerns over data security and privacy. A significant portion of organizations report that AI is not relevant to their business, and others cite cybersecurity or privacy concerns as major barriers. ([aicanadapulse.ca](https://www.aicanadapulse.ca/adoption?utm_source=openai))

   - **Workforce Readiness:** While the policy aims to create numerous AI-related job opportunities, there is a pressing need to ensure that the existing workforce possesses the necessary skills to fill these roles. A substantial number of organizations lack dedicated governance functions to manage AI risks, and many leaders anticipate positive financial outcomes from trustworthy AI, viewing it as a value driver rather than a cost center. ([pwc.com](https://www.pwc.com/ca/en/media/release/pwc-canada-2026-trust-in-ai-report.html?utm_source=openai))

   - **Integration Challenges:** The successful adoption of AI requires seamless integration into existing workflows and infrastructure. Many organizations report difficulties in this area, citing challenges such as unclear ownership, difficulty inventorying existing AI systems, and fears that responsible AI will slow innovation. ([pwc.com](https://www.pwc.com/ca/en/media/release/pwc-canada-2026-trust-in-ai-report.html?utm_source=openai))

3. **Suggested solutions or approaches:**
   To enhance the effectiveness of this policy and address the identified challenges, the following measures are recommended:

   - **Comprehensive Training Programs:** Develop and implement training initiatives that not only focus on technical AI skills but also emphasize responsible AI practices, data governance, and ethical considerations. This approach will prepare the workforce to manage AI technologies effectively and ethically. ([kpmg.com](https://kpmg.com/ca/en/insights/2026/03/responsible-ai-adoption-in-canadian-public-sector.html?utm_source=openai))

   - **Support for SMEs:** Provide targeted assistance to SMEs to facilitate AI adoption. This could include financial incentives, access to AI expertise, and resources to help integrate AI into their operations. Such support is crucial, as SMEs often lack the resources to adopt AI independently. ([mitacs.ca](https://www.mitacs.ca/our-innovation-insights/closing-the-ai-impact-gap/?utm_source=openai))

   - **Strengthening Governance Frameworks:** Establish clear governance structures to oversee AI initiatives, ensuring accountability and transparency. This includes defining roles and responsibilities, setting standards for AI deployment, and monitoring outcomes to build trust among stakeholders. ([pwc.com](https://www.pwc.com/ca/en/media/release/pwc-canada-2026-trust-in-ai-report.html?utm_source=openai))

   - **Addressing Data Security and Privacy Concerns:** Implement robust data protection measures and transparent policies to alleviate concerns related to data security and privacy. Ensuring that AI systems are secure and that personal data is handled responsibly will encourage broader adoption. ([aicanadapulse.ca](https://www.aicanadapulse.ca/adoption?utm_source=openai))

   - **Fostering Collaboration:** Encourage collaboration between government bodies, educational institutions, industry leaders, and community organizations to create a cohesive strategy for AI adoption. Such partnerships can facilitate knowledge sharing, resource pooling, and the development of best practices. ([pm.gc.ca](https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/news/news-releases/2026/06/04/prime-minister-carney-launches-ai-all-canadas-new-national-artificial?utm_source=openai))

   By implementing these measures, the policy can more effectively address the barriers to AI adoption and contribute to a more robust and inclusive AI ecosystem in Canada.
